task: Variational, finite-element, spectral, adaptive, parabolic and mixed numerical PDE coverage
scope: Galerkin and finite element methods for elliptic PDEs
mesh regularity, interpolation, quadrature and a priori/a posteriori error estimates
mixed methods and inf-sup stability, including Stokes discretizations
parabolic variational theory and FEM in space and time
compact elliptic eigenproblems and spectral/pseudospectral approximation
adaptive finite element convergence and complexity
numerical incompressible flow, with the 3D global Navier-Stokes problem kept separate

areas.external_status: Established results; proof obligations are standard, not open problems.
source_coverage: Guermond Chapters 24–27, 2019 Chapters 32–33, and the relevant interpolation chapters were read in full. Clason Chapter 9 was read for mixed methods; it is not the source of the conforming elliptic FEM claims listed here.

The model Poisson problem is posed on a bounded Lipschitz/polyhedral domain with H^1_0 trial/test space. For symmetric coercive a, the conforming Galerkin solution is the energy projection and satisfies Céa/quasi-optimality; for nonsymmetric coercive forms the constant is continuity/coercivity.

Piecewise polynomial rates require an affine, matching mesh family with uniform shape regularity and a stated local approximation operator. For u in H^{1+r}, degree k, the H^1 error is O(h^r), 0≤r≤k. The L^2 Aubin–Nitsche gain is h^s only when the adjoint solution has H^{1+s} regularity; h^{r+1} requires s=1.
areas.proof_route: Weak formulation and Lax–Milgram → Galerkin orthogonality → best-approximation estimate → Bramble–Hilbert/Deny–Lions plus mesh scaling for interpolation → dual adjoint problem for the L^2 bound.
important_hypotheses: bounded sesquilinear/bilinear form and uniform coercivity on the trial space; for mixed or Petrov settings use a discrete inf-sup condition instead
conformity V_h⊂V for the plain Céa statement
shape-regular affine meshes; matching interfaces for the source estimates used here
Sobolev regularity of u and, for duality, a separately stated adjoint regularity pickup
areas.local_gap: No local mesh/reference-element definitions, Bramble–Hilbert estimate, interpolation operator, Céa theorem for a finite-dimensional Galerkin space, Ritz projection, or FEM error-rate theorem was found.

areas.area: Mesh interpolation, inverse estimates, quadrature and variational crimes
source_coverage: Guermond Chapter 8 specifies matching affine mesh coverage and mesh geometry; Chapter 11 states a shape-regularity ratio h_K/rho_K≤sigma and proves local interpolation estimates through a reference-cell operator; Chapter 12 gives inverse and discrete trace inequalities.

Guermond 2019 Chapters 32–33 give H^1-conforming approximation, inhomogeneous boundary lifting, and quadrature perturbation conditions. Exact quadrature or a variational-crime estimate is needed; the quadrature theorem requires polynomial degree, quadrature order, coefficient regularity and a small-mesh/stability condition.

Pointwise Lagrange interpolation requires enough Sobolev regularity for nodal values. For weaker regularity the source uses averaged quasi-interpolation or an L^2 projection; these are different operators with different assumptions.
areas.proof_route: Reference-cell mapping and finite-dimensional norm equivalence → Deny–Lions/Bramble–Hilbert approximation → scaling by the affine Jacobian → trace/inverse estimates under shape regularity → Strang perturbation estimate for quadrature or nonconformity.
important_hypotheses: uniformly bounded element-map condition numbers / shape regularity
polynomial reproduction and boundedness of the chosen local interpolation functional
nodal interpolation only above the relevant Sobolev embedding threshold
quadrature order and coefficient regularity explicitly matched to the target rate
areas.local_gap: No mesh shape-regularity, local reference-map, Bramble–Hilbert, finite-element inverse/trace, Fortin interpolation, quadrature consistency, or Strang variational-crime supplier was found. The local sharp trace theorem is only for bounded C^1 domains and 1<p<∞; it does not supply polyhedral face inverse estimates.

areas.area: Nonconforming elliptic methods: Crouzeix–Raviart, Nitsche and SIP-DG
areas.external_status: Established under explicit consistency, coercivity and regularity hypotheses.
source_coverage: Guermond Chapters 36–38 were read completely. CR uses piecewise affine functions with zero mean jumps on interior faces and zero boundary face means; the broken gradient norm is coercive, with discrete Poincare and jump bounds.
Nitsche's method requires a penalty gamma(h_F)=gamma_0/h_F above a trace-constant threshold; consistency plus stability yields a quasi-optimal broken energy error.

SIP-DG requires a matching shape-regular affine mesh, polynomial degree k≥1, jump penalty gamma_0/h_F, and gamma_0 above the inverse-trace threshold. Exact consistency and adjoint consistency support energy and L^2 estimates. The L^2 rate is limited by the elliptic regularity index s; non-symmetric/incomplete variants can lose the adjoint-consistency gain.
areas.proof_route: Define a broken energy norm → prove discrete coercivity via inverse trace inequality and penalty threshold → integrate the exact PDE by parts cellwise for consistency → bound consistency defect in a larger comparison norm → apply the abstract nonconforming Strang lemma → use a dual problem for L^2 error.
important_hypotheses: cellwise polynomial approximation and controlled face jumps
penalty scaled like h_F^{-1} with a method-specific threshold
for CR energy analysis, u∈H^{1+r} with r>1/2 so normal-derivative traces are defined
for L^2 error, adjoint elliptic smoothing H^{1+s}, s>1/2 in the displayed source result
areas.local_gap: No local FE definitions or theorem carriers for CR, Nitsche, SIP-DG, broken norms, penalty coercivity, Strang consistency, flux recovery or DG eigenapproximation were found.

areas.area: A posteriori estimation and adaptive FEM
areas.external_status: Established reliability, efficiency and convergence results under method-specific assumptions; optimal complexity is conditional and not universal.
source_coverage: Nochetto Lectures 1–4 were read completely. For linear elliptic problems the residual estimator combines element residuals h_K^2||R_K||^2 and face flux jumps h_F||J_F||^2; a local lower bound includes data oscillation.
Dorfler bulk marking plus mesh refinement that creates interior nodes yields error reduction in the symmetric model. Oscillation must be reduced separately for rough data.

For nonsymmetric convection forms, quasi-orthogonality is perturbative and the convergence theorem assumes an initial mesh sufficiently fine relative to ||b||; a combined error/oscillation quantity contracts.

The optimal-complexity result for the simplest case assumes the Laplacian, P1, piecewise constant f and membership in an approximation class. The more general coefficient-dependent optimality theorem is stated with proof referred to an external paper; it must not be advertised as a proved universal result from these four notes.
areas.proof_route: Elementwise integration by parts → residual representation → Clément approximation and trace estimates for reliability → element/face bubble functions for local efficiency up to oscillation → Dörfler marking and refinement reduction → orthogonality/quasi-orthogonality plus oscillation contraction → approximation-class and bisection complexity arguments.
important_hypotheses: ellipticity, coefficient regularity or coefficient oscillation terms, and source data class stated
shape-regular conforming triangulations and a refinement rule with a uniform reduction factor
oscillation controlled alongside residual indicators
for nonsymmetric convection, the stated small-initial-mesh condition
optimal complexity requires a specified approximation class and mesh-closure/complexity estimates
areas.local_gap: No residual estimator, reliability/efficiency theorem, Dörfler marking, adaptive convergence, mesh-closure, or approximation-class complexity result is local.

areas.external_status: Established under the Babuška–Brezzi conditions; stable pairs are mesh- and dimension-sensitive.
source_coverage: Guermond Chapter 49 §49.4 and Chapter 50 provide the abstract kernel-coercivity plus constraint inf-sup conditions, Fortin operator transfer, mixed Céa estimate, Schur complement and solver proofs. Clason Chapter 9 independently gives the Brezzi splitting/Fortin criterion and Raviart–Thomas mixed Poisson construction.

Guermond Chapters 53–55 derive Stokes weak well-posedness from Korn coercivity and surjectivity of divergence, then show the discrete problem is well-posed iff the discrete divergence inf-sup constant is positive. Error bounds carry beta_h and the Fortin norm; pressure robustness is tied to ker(B_h)⊂ker(B).

Reviewed stable examples include mini (P1+bubble,P1), Taylor–Hood (P2,P1), selected higher-order pairs, Scott–Vogelius on specified non-singular/specially refined meshes, (P2,P0) in 2D, (P2-bubble,P1-discontinuous), and Crouzeix–Raviart/P0. The sources also construct checkerboard modes for unstable Q1/P0 and P1/P1, and explain P1/P0 locking.
areas.proof_route: For continuous Stokes, use Korn plus a bounded right inverse of divergence; for discrete stability, prove a uniform inf-sup by Fortin preservation, pressure-gradient control, or macroelement decomposition. Then apply mixed error estimates and explicit approximation rates.
important_hypotheses: velocity space enforces essential boundary data and pressure normalization/mean-zero compatibility is correct
uniform discrete inf-sup constant beta_0>0, not merely solvability on one mesh
stable pair results retain their dimension, mesh geometry, polynomial degree, and boundary hypotheses
smoothness-dependent rates require exact and adjoint Stokes regularity; nonsmooth domains lower rates
areas.local_gap: No local Babuška–Brezzi theorem, divergence right inverse, Korn inequality, Fortin lemma, mixed Galerkin theorem, stable Stokes pair, pressure-robustness result, or mixed error estimate was found.

areas.area: Parabolic variational theory and finite elements
areas.external_status: Established well-posedness and stability under evolution-triple, measurability, boundedness and coercivity assumptions; error rates need added spatial/time regularity.
source_coverage: Clason Chapters 11–12 provide the Gelfand triple V↪H↪V*, W(0,T;V)↪C([0,T];H), weak time integration by parts, BNB well-posedness, and cG/dG time-space methods.

Long Chen's full note develops heat-equation energy estimates, semidiscrete FEM stability, Ritz projection error equation, duality-based L2 superconvergence, and Euler/CN and time-Galerkin methods. The note explicitly assumes well-posedness by reference to Evans rather than proving it.

Time-discontinuous Galerkin stability and endpoint error estimates require a coercive symmetric spatial form, a finite-dimensional polynomial-in-time space, jump terms and stated temporal/spatial regularity; the general variable-space/time-dependent case is referred elsewhere.
areas.proof_route: Evolution-triple trace theorem and integration-by-parts identity → BNB for space-time bilinear form → test by u for energy stability → Ritz projection and commuting consistency identity for semidiscrete error → dual backward problem for L2 estimates → time-polynomial approximation plus dG jump energy for fully discrete estimates.
important_hypotheses: V reflexive/dense in H and continuous embedding H↪V*
a(t;·,·) measurable, uniformly bounded and coercive a.e.
initial datum in H with trace meaningful through W(0,T;V)↪C([0,T];H)
spatial elliptic regularity, time derivatives, and initial projection error explicitly tracked
areas.local_gap: The local semigroup suppliers do not provide the evolution-triple variational existence theorem, spatial Galerkin stability/error estimates, Ritz projection identity, time discretization theorem, or a posteriori estimate. No general finite-element parabolic theorem was found.

areas.external_status: Established approximation theory under compactness, stability, conformity/consistency, and smoothness assumptions.
source_coverage: Guermond Chapters 46–47 treat compact self-adjoint solution operators, conforming symmetric eigenvalue approximation, min-max, upper bounds, and eigenfunction/eigenvalue estimates. For fixed eigenvalue index m and sufficiently small h, conforming Galerkin eigenvalues are upper bounds and the eigenvalue error is quadratic in the best energy approximation; smoothness can give double the H1 eigenfunction rate.

Chapter 48 applies compact-operator perturbation to nonsymmetric, multiple and nonconforming eigenproblems. It requires operator norm convergence, uniform discrete stability, primal/adjoint smoothing and approximation on generalized eigenspaces; eigenvalue average, eigenspace gap and individual eigenvector estimates have distinct exponents involving ascent and adjoint regularity.

Shen–Tang Chapters 2–3 and §1.8 provide polynomial collocation/Galerkin constructions, weighted Sobolev approximation, boundary treatment, quadrature, conditioning and higher-order/Petrov examples. Exponential rates require analytic/sufficiently smooth data and appropriate nodes; periodic Fourier collocation assumes periodicity.
areas.proof_route: Continuous compact solution operator via Rellich → compact self-adjoint spectral theorem or compact nonnormal operator perturbation → Galerkin operator convergence from primal and adjoint approximation → spectral gap/min-max or generalized-eigenspace perturbation → weighted polynomial interpolation/projection estimates for spectral rates.
important_hypotheses: compactness of the continuous solution operator; for the local Dirichlet setting, bounded-domain Rellich compactness is available for H^1_0
conforming symmetric Ritz eigenproblems for guaranteed upper bounds
for Babuška–Osborn rates, operator norm convergence and both primal/adjoint regularity indices are required
spectral polynomial rates depend on regularity class, boundary treatment, nodes/weights and quadrature exactness
areas.local_gap: The continuous operator/eigenbasis/min-max suppliers exist, but no local finite-element eigenvalue/eigenfunction convergence theorem, Babuška–Osborn perturbation theorem, spectral collocation/Galerkin approximation theorem, weighted polynomial interpolation estimate, or aliasing/dealiasing result was found.

areas.area: Navier–Stokes global smoothness versus numerical flow methods
areas.external_status: CMI problem remains officially marked Active in the fetched official page; a 2026 announcement reports that it apparently has been settled but provides no proof details or identified alternative in the article. Status is pending verification, not an established theorem.
source_coverage: The original official CMI statement asks for one of four exact alternatives A–D: global smoothness for unforced data on R^3 or the periodic torus, or a forced breakdown example on the corresponding domain.

The same statement records established adjacent results: 2D global smoothness, 3D small-data global smoothness, 3D arbitrary-data local smoothness, Leray weak existence, and Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg partial regularity. None is the full 3D global claim.
Stokes FE theory and periodic Fourier pseudospectral computations are separate numerical/existence topics and do not prove or discharge the CMI global regularity statement.
areas.exact_claim_boundary: Keep the smooth 3D global existence/breakdown alternative separate from Stokes solvability, local-in-time strong solutions, 2D global regularity, small-data global regularity, Leray weak solutions, and numerical simulations.
areas.local_gap: No local Navier–Stokes weak-solution, local-strong-solution, 2D global, regularity criterion, partial-regularity, or 3D global-regularity result was found. Do not make any numerical method or CMI announcement a logical supplier to the open problem.

source_specific_non_open_proof_gap.claim: A second-order consistent pressure-splitting scheme for unsteady Navier–Stokes has a second-order error estimate.
source_specific_non_open_proof_gap.source_observation: Shen–Tang §7.4 reports numerical evidence for second-order accuracy and says a rigorous proof was unavailable at the time of writing.
source_specific_non_open_proof_gap.classification: Historical source-limited proof gap. Its current research status was not independently established here; do not classify it as a recognized open problem or an established theorem from this source alone.

reusable_local_foundation: Use the published local weak-Sobolev, zero-boundary closure, Poincare, Lax–Milgram and weak Dirichlet Poisson statements for the common elliptic variational prelude.
Use the local Rellich, compact self-adjoint, symmetric elliptic operator and Courant–Fischer statements for continuous eigenproblem foundations.
Use the local analytic heat semigroup and abstract sectorial-semigroup statements only for continuous semigroup claims; do not present them as finite-element convergence suppliers.
numerical_prose_reuse.reuse_boundary: Numerical prose may explain established algorithms and source theorems, but a literature citation or source chapter is not a local proof dependency. A claim becomes a logical supplier only after the library has an exact published carrier with matching hypotheses.

coverage_gaps_summary: Mesh, finite-element, interpolation, quadrature and inverse-estimate definitions/theorems are absent locally.
No local Galerkin/Cea/Strang, residual a posteriori, AFEM, mixed inf-sup/Fortin/Stokes, parabolic FEM, or finite-element/spectral eigenapproximation theorem exists.
